ops.expect: The White Chuck approach described below is effectively gone: White Chuck River Trail #643 has been listed as inaccessible since the 2003 flood, and the White Chuck Road (FR 23) is closed to vehicles at milepost 3.7, about 5 miles of old roadbed short of the old trailhead, beyond which the valley is unmaintained travel with a river ford. Parties now come in from the North Fork Sauk River Trailhead instead, climbing to the Pacific Crest Trail at White Pass and following it north over Red Pass to the Sitkum Creek junction. From the White Chuck River Trailhead (2,350 ft, end of White Chuck River Road/FR 23), follow the White Chuck River Trail (FST 643) upstream through old-growth forest. The trail fords/bridges several tributaries — Pumice Creek, Glacier Creek, and Kennedy Creek — which serve as reliable water sources but can run high with snowmelt in early summer. At about 5.5 miles reach the former Kennedy Hot Springs/Kennedy Guard Station area (~3,300 ft) — still a popular campsite, but the historic hot-springs pool, lodge, and guard station were destroyed and buried by the October 2003 flood/debris flow and were never rebuilt; there is no usable hot pool here. Continue roughly 1.5 miles farther to Sitkum Creek and the junction with the Pacific Crest Trail (~3,850 ft). Turn north (left) on the PCT for about a half mile to a forested campsite near 4,100 ft — a common lower camp. From there, leave the maintained trail and follow a steep, unmaintained climbers' path (locally described as 'more like a fisherman's route than a trail') straight up the forested ridge to Boulder Basin (5,500–6,000 ft), where the trees break and the standard high camp sits on heather/rock benches with running water nearby. From camp, ascend snowfields southeast/uphill onto the toe of the Sitkum Glacier. Note: the White Chuck River Road and Trail sustained major washout damage in the October 2003 floods and has had repeated closures/repairs since — confirm current road-end and trail status with the Mount Baker-Snoqualmie National Forest before relying on this approach, as in bad years the effective trailhead moves miles downstream.
ops.value: From the North Fork Sauk River Trailhead (off Sloan Creek Road, FR 49), follow North Fork Sauk Trail #649 up the valley through old-growth forest, past the Red Creek bridge to Mackinaw Shelter, then up a long series of switchbacks to meet the Pacific Crest Trail at about 5,950 ft, roughly 8-9 miles from the car. White Pass and its camp are a short way south along the PCT; this route does not go there. Turn north on the PCT and cross Red Pass (about 6,500 ft) a mile or two on, then descend into the upper White Chuck valley and follow the PCT down it for roughly 7-9 miles, past the old White Chuck River Trail junction (~3,850 ft), to a forested campsite near 4,100 ft beside Sitkum Creek. There, leave the maintained trail on the unsigned, unmaintained climbers' path (locally described as 'more like a fisherman's route than a trail'), which goes straight up the forested ridge south of Sitkum Creek to Boulder Basin (5,500-6,000 ft), where the trees break and the standard high camp sits on heather and rock benches with running water nearby. From camp, ascend snowfields southeast onto the toe of the Sitkum Glacier. The old approach up the White Chuck River Trail past Kennedy Hot Springs to the same PCT junction is no longer usable: the White Chuck Road (FR 23) is closed to vehicles at milepost 3.7, and the trail has been listed as inaccessible since the October 2003 flood. Going out, the PCT climbs back up the valley and over Red Pass before the long descent to the car.

expect.name: White Chuck River Trail #643 (the historic standard)
expect.notes:
This was the standard way up Glacier Peak and the road access has been unreliable for a very long time. The last several miles of FR 23 to the White Chuck trailhead have been reported blocked — at one point with large boulders placed at the turnoff — and reports of the road being driveable and undriveable have alternated over the years. Confirm with the Mount Baker-Snoqualmie forest before relying on it, because in a bad year the effective trailhead moves miles downstream.

From the trailhead at about 2,350 ft the trail runs upstream through old growth, crossing Pumice, Glacier and Kennedy Creeks — reliable water, but high with snowmelt in early summer. At about five and a half miles is the old Kennedy Hot Springs area at around 3,300 ft, still a popular campsite; the pool, lodge and guard station were destroyed by the 2003 flood and never rebuilt, so there is no usable hot pool there.

Another mile and a half brings you to Sitkum Creek and the PCT junction at about 3,850 ft. Turn north on the PCT for about half a mile to a forested camp near 4,100 ft.
hazards: unreliable road access to the trailhead over many years
creek fords running high with early-summer snowmelt
steep unmaintained climbers' path with no signage leaving the PCT
expect.baseFinding:
The path that leaves the PCT for Boulder Basin is unsigned and steeper than anything before it — climbers describe it as more of a fisherman's track than a trail. The test is direction, not appearance: the correct path goes STRAIGHT UP the forested ridge. Anything that contours is the PCT or a game trail.

You know you have arrived at the top of it when the trees break: Boulder Basin at roughly 5,500 to 6,000 ft is heather and rock benches with running water, and it is the standard high camp. If you are still in continuous forest, you are below it, however long the climb has felt.

From camp the route ascends snowfields onto the toe of the Sitkum. Rope up at the point the snowfield stops being a slope you can see the bottom of and becomes continuous glacier — there is no rock landmark for this, so the transition is judged on the ground rather than found.

expect.name: North Fork Sauk and the PCT (the reliable alternative)
expect.notes: Because the White Chuck side has been unreliable for years, parties reach this side of the mountain instead from the North Fork Sauk River trailhead, climbing to White Pass on the PCT and then travelling north over Red Pass toward the Glacier Creek and Sitkum ground. It is substantially longer and is chosen for access rather than for the climbing.
hazards: very long approach on the PCT with substantial gain and loss
no signed junction for the climbers' path
expect.baseFinding: The route above is unchanged: the marker is Boulder Basin — trees giving way to heather and rock benches with running water at roughly 5,500 to 6,000 ft — and then snowfields onto the toe of the Sitkum above it. Arriving from the north on the PCT the risk is passing the drainage entirely, so identify the Sitkum Creek and Glacier Creek junctions on the map before you set out rather than expecting signage.

value.name: North Fork Sauk Trail and the PCT over Red Pass
value.notes: The way in since the White Chuck side closed. North Fork Sauk Trail #649 runs up the valley through old growth to Mackinaw Shelter and then switchbacks steeply to the Pacific Crest Trail at about 5,950 ft, roughly eight to nine miles from the trailhead. Turn north on the PCT, cross Red Pass a mile or two on, and descend into the upper White Chuck valley, following the PCT down it for roughly seven to nine miles past the old White Chuck River Trail junction to Sitkum Creek. It is much longer than the old approach, and the climb back over Red Pass comes on the way out.
hazards: very long approach on the PCT with substantial gain and loss
no signed junction for the climbers' path
value.baseFinding: The route above is unchanged: the marker is Boulder Basin — trees giving way to heather and rock benches with running water at roughly 5,500 to 6,000 ft — and then snowfields onto the toe of the Sitkum above it. Coming down the valley on the PCT the risk is walking past the start of the climbers' path, so mark the old White Chuck River Trail junction and Sitkum Creek on the map before you set out rather than expecting signage.

creek fords running high with early-summer snowmelt

sectionBreakdown.note: Follow the PCT down the upper White Chuck valley to Sitkum Creek, then take the steep, unsigned climbers' path up the ridge south of the creek to the high camp at Boulder Basin.
sectionBreakdown.fromTo: Down the PCT to Sitkum Creek and up to Boulder Basin

sectionBreakdown.note: Rope up from Boulder Basin, climb the heavily crevassed Sitkum Glacier to a saddle near Sitkum Spire (~9,500 ft), then follow the pumice/scree ridge (with one short snow traverse) …
Break camp, descend the climbers' path to the PCT, and walk back up the White Chuck valley and over Red Pass to the North Fork Sauk Trail and the trailhead.

ops.expect: Follow the White Chuck River Trail about 5.5 miles to the old Kennedy Hot Springs site, then 1.5 miles more to Sitkum Creek and the PCT. Go north on the PCT about half a mile to a forest camp near 4,100 ft, then take the steep, unmaintained climbers' path up the ridge south of Sitkum Creek to Boulder Basin (5,500–6,000 ft), the usual high camp. Confirm road and trail status before going.
ops.value: Follow North Fork Sauk Trail #649 to the Pacific Crest Trail, go north over Red Pass and down the upper White Chuck valley on the PCT to Sitkum Creek, then take the steep, unmaintained climbers' path from a forest camp near 4,100 ft up the ridge south of the creek to Boulder Basin (5,500–6,000 ft), the usual high camp.

ops.find: From Boulder Basin, follow the steep climbers' path back down to the PCT/White Chuck Trail junction and retrace the White Chuck River Trail to the trailhead.
ops.replace: From Boulder Basin, follow the steep climbers' path back down to the PCT at Sitkum Creek, then walk the PCT back up the White Chuck valley and over Red Pass to the North Fork Sauk Trail and the trailhead.

ops.expect: The White Chuck River Trail has been unmaintained and washed out since the October 2003 flood, which adds significant off-trail travel on that approach
ops.value: A very long approach that crosses Red Pass both ways; the old White Chuck River Trail has been listed as inaccessible since the October 2003 flood

ops.expect: If the White Chuck River Road/Trail is washed out or closed, most parties instead reach Boulder Basin via the North Fork Sauk Trail to White Pass and a cross-country traverse into the Glacier Peak basins.
ops.value: The White Chuck River Road and Trail are closed, so parties reach Boulder Basin from the North Fork Sauk Trail and the PCT, over Red Pass and down the upper White Chuck valley.

ops.find: It is about ten miles from the road end, and the road itself has a long history of washouts, so confirm where the trailhead actually is before you plan the day.
ops.replace: It sits at the end of a long approach from the North Fork Sauk trailhead, over Red Pass and down the upper White Chuck valley on the PCT, so plan the walk in as a trip of its own.

ops.find: The lowest planned stop, about 5.5 miles in and still widely used.
ops.replace: Not on the current approach: this site is on the White Chuck River Trail below its junction with the PCT, and that trail has been listed as inaccessible since the 2003 flood.

ops.find: Useful as a first night for parties splitting the approach, or as a retreat in bad weather, but it is a long way and a lot of gain below the glacier.
ops.replace: Parties coming over Red Pass do not pass it.

pin.name: North Fork Sauk Trail / PCT junction
pin.note: Top of the North Fork Sauk switchbacks. Turn north on the PCT here for Red Pass and the White Chuck valley; White Pass is a short way south and off this route.
